key_insight: Combining LLM-driven natural-language communication with conformal prediction lets heterogeneous robots coordinate more efficiently by only exchanging high-confidence, task-relevant messages—reducing bandwidth and improving reliability.
problem_solved: Enables robust multi-robot coordination for complex, language-specified assignments where agents must gather information, ask/answer scene questions, and allocate manipulation tasks under limited or noisy communication.
method: Use LLMs to generate & interpret natural-language plans, questions, and answers for scene understanding and task allocation across heterogeneous agents.
Apply conformal prediction to produce calibrated confidence scores for LLM outputs and filter/flag low-confidence messages before transmission or execution.
Design a lightweight communication protocol that transmits concise, high-confidence assertions and targeted queries to minimize bandwidth and reduce erroneous actions.
impact: Provides a practical framework for deploying LLM-enabled multi-robot systems in real-world, bandwidth-constrained settings—improving coordination efficiency and safety by making communication selective and uncertainty-aware.
visual_elements: Architecture diagram: multiple robot agents + onboard LLM modules + conformal prediction filter + central or peer-to-peer comms links.
Sequence flow: example task showing question generation, confidence scoring, filtered message passing, and task assignment.
Bar/line chart: messages transmitted vs. task success or completion time comparing standard LLM comms vs. CommCP (shows reduced traffic with maintained/improved success).
Icon set: heterogeneous robots (arm, gripper, mobile), speech/chat bubbles with confidence badges, and a warning flag for low-confidence outputs.
paper_title: CommCP: Efficient Multi-Agent Coordination via LLM-Based Communication with Conformal Prediction
paper_authors: Xiaopan Zhang, Zejin Wang, Zhixu Li, Jianpeng Yao, Jiachen Li
